title: Epilogue: The Truth About the Dance

A_open.text: Thanksgiving weekend. The first snow of the year blankets the McVine farm in white.

then.text: Patch Seven is quiet under the snow. No glow. No hum. Just a field.

else.text: Patch Seven glows very faintly under the snow. Like a night-light for the whole field.

A_open.text: In the yard, Gord is talking to Doris, who is wearing a scarf.
Brad's father is coming. Be polite.
A rented car crunches up the drive. A tall man in a too-thin coat steps out, carrying six pies.
Hi, buddy. I brought pie. Six of them. Don't look at me like that.
These are apple. I'm not a monster.
The two men hug, awkwardly, for a very long time. Doris looks on.

B_story.text: The farmhouse kitchen. Six pies. Three men. One enormous, overdue story.
Brad. I owe you the truth about the dance.
I've heard five versions. Quarterback. Mascot. Lab rat.
The quarterback story was mine. I thought it was a good one.
It was terrible. Nobody believed you could throw.
I threw a ball over the chapel!
You threw a crow.
The mascot story was Gord's. The 'never attended a game' story is true.
We made up stories so nobody would settle on one. Eleanor's idea. She was clever.
Twenty-five years ago, Gord's back field grew pumpkins that did something strange.
Eat one, and you told the truth. For about ten minutes. We were thrilled.
I suggested using them at the Halloween dance.
No, I did.
You didn't. I did. You were busy staring at a girl.
...That part's true.
The Great Hall, twenty-five years ago. A full moon, a glowing punch bowl, and the program banner.
The whole student body went candid at once. Forty-one fights. Nine proposals. A casserole brawl.
The casserole survived.
Your mother was there. I'd stared at her for a year and never said a word.
I drank the punch. I walked across the floor. I said: 'I'm in love with you and I'm terrified.'
She said: 'I know. You've been staring at me for a year.'
Very loud. The whole hall heard.
Best night of my life. Worst night of the program.
The college shut it down. Eleanor took all the blame. She sealed the samples and resigned.
We promised to bury it. To protect her name. It was the only thing we could give her.
The pumpkins bloom when a full moon falls on Halloween. It happened then. It happened this year.
I couldn't be here. I couldn't tell you. So I sent you to Gord. Someone I trusted.
And honestly? I hoped you wouldn't find out.
You hoped I wouldn't find out?
I hoped. I failed. I'm proud.

do.text: You lied to me. For eighteen years.
You told me you were 'Ravenwood's best arm'.
I'm still angry. But I'm very glad I'm here.
You were protecting people. I understand.
Daniel's eyes shine. He wipes them with a corner of a pie box.
You're a better man than I was at eighteen.
So I'm the product of a pumpkin-induced confession. I'm basically a squash.
You have your mother's sense of humor.

then.text: On the kitchen windowsill sits a small clay pot. Gord quietly nudges it into the light.
One seed. For luck.
Gordon.
One.

else.text: I saw a poster at the station. WARNING: NEXT YEAR'S DANCE MAY CONTAIN HONESTY.
The Dean's idea. He's very afraid of squirrels.

B_story.text: Eat your pie.
Three men eat apple pie in a kitchen full of snow light. Nobody says anything for a while.

then.text: At the cafe, I couldn't say no and you asked anyway. I've decided you meant well.
You asked me a question I couldn't refuse. I said yes. I'm... actually glad I did.

else.text: You asked about the program while I couldn't refuse. I haven't forgotten. I have forgiven.

v_j.text: Snow on the farm. Jane, in her work jacket, cheeks pink, waves from the middle of the yard.
Help me build a snow pumpkin. A big one. For Doris's friends.
They roll it, stack it, and prop it up. It is a lumpy, optimistic pumpkin.
I'm staying. I'll study agronomy at Ravenwood and take over the farm. On my own terms.

then.text: And I'd like you here.
She presses a key into his hand. It's cold and heavy.
Barn key. Dad had it made. He says it means you're staff.
Under the lumpy snow pumpkin, in the quiet snow, Jane kisses him.

else.text: Ask me again after the harvest.
They lean against the snow pumpkin and watch the sun set over the white field.

v_s.text: Trivia night at the Log and Stump. Brad has joined Sandra's team. They are called The Stumped.
Final round. Pumpkins. Don't embarrass us.
Question ten! What is the powerhouse of the cell?
The entire tavern groans. The Stumped lose by ten points.
Sandra puts her face in her hands. Her shoulders shake. Then she looks up, smiling. A full, real smile.
Around the bar, regulars gasp. Money changes hands.
I'm smiling because we lost. Not because of you.

then.text: Behind the bar, the old photo of three researchers now hangs beside a new one: Brad and Sandra.
Don't let it go to your head. It's a small frame.
Sandra takes his hand under the table. For once, nobody bets against it.

else.text: Come back next week. Bring brains.
She leans on the table next to him. It's close, but not quite touching. For now.

v_g.text: The Grove Cafe. A new chalkboard: PUMPKIN SURPRISE, HONEST EDITION. (NO GLOW. NO CONFESSIONS.)
Brad! First taster! You're the only one who tells me the truth!
He takes a bite. It's warm, sweet, and wholly ordinary, in the best way.
That's what I was going for!

then.text: I mailed it, you know. The envelope. I start pastry school in January.
When I go to the city, I want the cafe to be a little bit yours too.
She sets a brass key on the counter, next to a tart.
A key to the cafe?
And I'm coming home every weekend. You'd better be waiting. With coffee.
Across the counter, Georgia leans in and kisses him. The tart goes untouched, for once.

else.text: Help me plan the city trip? Maps, bakeries, snacks. You carry the snacks.
They spend the morning drawing a map of the best bakeries in a city neither of them has seen.

v_p.text: December. Grades are filed. A knock at the farmhouse door.
Patricia stands on the porch in her trench coat. No mustache. A thermos in her hand.
Mr. Bart. Grades are filed. I am, technically, no longer your professor this term.

then.text: You may ask me again.
Patricia. Would you like to have dinner with me?
Yes. Yes, I would.
She pulls a pair of safety goggles from her coat and puts them on.
Goggles?
I don't know what happens when I'm this happy.
Snow falls on the porch. In the doorway, Brad and Patricia share a very cautious, very warm kiss.

else.text: I would rather wait for spring. I'd like to do this properly.
She hands him the thermos. Cocoa, with a little cinnamon. For her, it is a declaration.

v_friends.text: Late afternoon on the steps of the Log and Stump. Someone has set up a camera on a timer.

then.text: Best friends. Forever. With pumpkin privileges.
Don't smile. If you smile, I'll end you.
Say 'muffin'! Say 'muffin' and mean it!

else.text: A photograph. Documentation of a most improbable semester.

v_friends.text: Brad, Jane, Sandra, Georgia, Patricia, and Gord on the steps. In the corner, the crow photobombs.
A good year. Kind of a weird one. But a good one.

v_farm.text: Winter at the farm. Brad has decided to stay, to see what a pumpkin farm is like when there are no pumpkins.
Lesson one. Winter pumpkins sleep. Don't wake them.
Lesson two. Never trust a goose.
One by one, over the weeks, the whole town stops by with stew.
Dad's soup is terrible. I brought a casserole.
Pumpkin ale. For the cold. And for the Admiral. He hates it.
Croissants! They're a little burnt! Honest Edition!
I was in the area. Birdwatching. The migratory ravens.

then.text: Not yet isn't never, farm boy.
I can wait. I'm very good at grudges. And at waiting.
I still have the envelope. Just in case you ever feel brave.

else.text: Ask me when you know, Mr. Bart. Or not at all. Either is acceptable.

v_farm.text: In the barn, Gord hands Brad a very small pumpkin. It hums, softly.
That night Gord slips a folded paper into Brad's pocket. Block capitals. A tiny pumpkin doodle.
On the porch rail, the crow looks on. Between Brad and Gord, a carved pumpkin glows in the snow.

D_credits.text: A visual novel for the Zeal 8-bit Computer
Starring Brad Bart, Jane McVine, Sandra Stump, Georgia Grove, and Prof. Patricia Peters
With Gord McVine, Daniel Bart, Doris, Linda, the Admiral, and a very patient crow
No pumpkins were harmed. Several were consulted.
On a snowy lamppost in Town Square, the crow sits wearing a tiny name tag: INSPECTOR (LEGACY!)
